sections.section_title: Initial Clinical Syndrome: Bacterial Sepsis and Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
sections.description: This section establishes the foundational clinical context, detailing the epidemiology of *Capnocytophaga canimorsus* infection, the initial presentation of overwhelming sepsis, and the management of DIC. It educates readers on the 'silent' sepsis course in immunocompetent hosts and the initial stabilization priorities before the TMA diagnosis is considered.
subtopics: Epidemiology of *Capnocytophaga canimorsus* and vector-specific exposure history (dog/cat bites)
Clinical presentation of community-acquired bacterial sepsis in adults
Identification of early septic shock markers: hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, and pancytopenia
Initial empiric antibiotic selection for zoonotic pathogens
Pathophysiology of Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) in sepsis vs. TMA

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Pivot: Recognizing and Defining Thrombotic Microangiopathy (TMA)
sections.description: This section focuses on the critical diagnostic shift from treating pure sepsis to identifying superimposed TMA. It guides the reader through the specific laboratory and clinical features of MAHA, thrombocytopenia, and renal failure, and rigorously walks through the exclusion of major mimics like TTP and STEC-HUS.
subtopics: Key clinical 'red flags' for TMA during a septic course (sudden hemolysis, worsening AKI)
Laboratory criteria for Microangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia (MAHA) and the significance of schistocytes
Diagnostic criteria and exclusion of Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) using ADAMTS13
Exclusion of Shiga-toxin associated HUS (STEC-HUS) via stool PCR and epidemiological history
Interpretation of the renal biopsy in the context of TMA and interpretation of complement levels (C3/C4)

sections.description: This section provides the underlying biological theory connecting *Capnocytophaga* infection to complement-mediated HUS. It explains the alternative complement pathway, the role of 'second hit' pathogens, and the nuances of hereditary versus acquired complement dysregulation without a clear genetic diagnosis.
subtopics: Overview of the Alternative Complement Pathway dysregulation in CM-HUS
The concept of 'Acquired' CM-HUS: Infection as a trigger in immunocompetent hosts
Specific virulence factors of *C. canimorsus* affecting endothelial activation and complement sensing
Why standard C3/C4 levels may remain normal during active CM-HUS
Interaction between complement inhibitors, bacterial capsules, and host defense mechanics

sections.section_title: Therapeutic Dilemma: Complement Blockade During Active Bacteraemia
sections.description: This section addresses the high-risk management challenges of treating CM-HUS with Eculizumab in the presence of active or recent infection. It discusses the risk/benefit ratio of blocking terminal complement components against encapsulated organisms and the strategy of bridging therapy versus early initiation.
subtopics: Indications and prioritization for early initiation of Eculizumab in TMA
Assessment of infectious risk specifically *C. canimorsus* and meningococcal disease after complement blockade
Role of Plasma Exchange (PEX) as a temporary bridge therapy versus definitive treatment
Prophylactic antibiotic strategies and the necessity of concomitant infection coverage
Vaccination protocols required prior to or during eculizumab maintenance therapy

sections.description: This final section evaluates the patient's recovery trajectory, separating hematological outcomes from renal outcomes. It generalizes the case lessons to broader medical practice, emphasizing the need for vigilance in distinguishing infectious triggers for HUS from idiopathic cases.
subtopics: Predictors of renal recovery in CM-HUS: the impact of Eculizumab timing
Differentiation between sustained hematological remission and renal fibrosis risk
Long-term follow-up requirements for patients on complement inhibitors
The importance of considering rare infectious triggers in undifferentiated TMA cases
Summary of clinical scoring tools and pathways for future TMA workups
